d: Shopping Jaraguá CENESP (part of Grupo Sol Panamby) is a premier commercial retail center operating within Latin America's largest business complex (Centro Empresarial de São Paulo - Cenesp). Serving tens of thousands of visitors daily with over 100 retail, dining, and service establishments, we blend decades of commercial excellence with forward-looking expansion strategies into emerging retail and mixed-use commercial markets globally.

We are seeking an analytical, proactive Market Entry Research Executive to lead regional market research and feasibility assessments as part of our strategic expansion initiatives. Operating remotely from Bahrain, you will gather and evaluate macroeconomic data, competitor dynamics, consumer trends, and commercial retail feasibility across regional target markets. You will turn raw market data into high-impact strategic insights that guide executive decision-making.
Conduct in-depth market research and feasibility studies to evaluate new market entry opportunities across the Middle East / GCC region.
Map competitor landscapes, analyze local consumer behaviors, and identify emerging retail, commercial, and customer demographic trends.
Design, coordinate, and execute qualitative and quantitative research methodologies, including surveys, stakeholder interviews, and data benchmarking.
Build and maintain structured research databases, market models, and competitive intelligence trackers.
Synthesize complex datasets into clear, executive-ready presentations, reports, and strategic recommendations for leadership.
Monitor regional macroeconomic policies, commercial retail regulations, and industry shifts that impact market entry viability.
Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Economics, Market Research, Statistics, Marketing, or a related quantitative field.
Proven track record in market research, commercial analytics, market entry consulting, or business intelligence (experience in retail, real estate, or commercial centers is an advantage).
Strong analytical mindset with hands-on proficiency in quantitative/qualitative analysis tools (advanced Excel, survey platforms, and data visualization tools).
Solid experience in designing questionnaires, structured survey methodologies, and data synthesis.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills in English; ability to present strategic findings clearly to cross-border teams.
High degree of self-motivation, organization, and capability to manage multiple research projects independently in a remote environment.
Competitive compensation benchmarked to regional standards.
100% remote flexibility with modern asynchronous collaboration tools.
Professional development allowance and career exposure within an established commercial group.
Annual performance incentive and generous paid time off (PTO).
Practical Case Exercise (Market entry evaluation & data interpretation)

As a Senior Cyber-Fraud Analyst, you are the expert owner of Deel Security’s fraud review quality. You handle the most complex and ambiguous cases, set the standard for how verdicts are reached and documented, and drive the improvements that make automated fraud detection more accurate. You also lead fraud research and red-team exercises, and act as the escalation point for the team’s hardest calls.

The work is detailed, high stakes and fast. A single verdict can protect a client from a fraudulent hire or wrongly cost a real candidate a job, so you combine precision with the judgment to decide when a case needs a different approach. You work independently, and you raise the bar for the analysts around you.
q: 6+ years in fraud investigation, fraud analysis, threat intelligence, trust and safety or identity verification operations, including experience working independently on complex cases.
Expert knowledge of identity fraud: fake and stolen identities, document fraud, synthetic identities and social engineering.
Proven ability to make and defend high-stakes calls under pressure, and to know when a case needs escalation or a different investigative approach.
Experience designing or refining detection signals, rules or review criteria based on case data.
Strong data skills: SQL to query and connect cases across datasets, with Python or scripting for analysis.
OSINT investigation skills and experience researching dark web or fraud-community sources safely.
Working knowledge of deepfakes, face swaps and voice cloning, and how they show up on video.
Experience coaching or mentoring other analysts, and a track record of raising the quality of a team’s work.
Clear, precise writing for both technical and non-technical audiences. Fluent English.
Experience with hiring fraud, remote worker fraud or state-backed IT worker schemes.
A QA, testing or security background, with a structured approach to breaking systems.
Hands-on experience with identity verification, liveness or deepfake detection tools.
Familiarity with ATS and HR systems.
Certifications such as CFE, or OSINT and threat intelligence credentials.
r: Own the review of complex, high-risk and ambiguous flagged candidates end to end: application, resume, contact details, interview recordings, identity verification results and AI investigation output.
Reach risk verdicts backed by clear evidence and reasoning, within the review SLA, and take escalations from the Cyber-Fraud Analyst team.
Detect sophisticated fraud patterns, including proxy interviews, deepfakes, face and voice mismatches, synthetic identities and coordinated applicants across clients.
Review the verdicts and case summaries of other analysts, give structured feedback, and correct the reasoning where needed.
Escalate systemic or high-impact cases to the FraudOps Team Lead with a clear recommendation.
Turn recurring fraud behaviour into concrete signals, rules and labelling guidance, and drive their validation with the product team.
Lead cross-case analysis of shared devices, emails, phone numbers, resume templates and interview behaviour to identify fraud rings.
Own review metrics (volume, turnaround time, false positives and false negatives), analyse the trends, and recommend actions to the Team Lead.
Scope and lead dark web and OSINT research on hiring fraud tools, services and fraud rings.
Design and run red-team scenarios against the verification flow (deepfake, document and proxy attempts), and document findings and remediation recommendations.
Assess new product features and vendors against realistic fraud scenarios before release.
Own the investigation playbooks and the fraud typology library, and keep them current as new fraud patterns emerge.
Lead the response to live fraud incidents, providing fast, accurate analysis and clear guidance to clients and internal teams.
Onboard and coach analysts on investigation methods, evidence standards and verdict writing.

Unit 42 - Unit 42 Consulting is Palo Alto Network's security advisory team. Our vision is to create a more secure digital world by providing the highest quality incident response, risk management, and digital forensic services to clients of all sizes. Our team is composed of recognized experts and incident responders with deep technical expertise and experience in investigations, data breach response, digital forensics, and information security. With a highly successful track record of delivering mission-critical cybersecurity solutions, we are experienced in working quickly to provide an effective incident response, attack readiness, and remediation plans with a focus on providing long-term support to improve our clients’ security posture.

The Senior Technical Project Manager on the Global Consulting Operations team will concurrently drive multiple cybersecurity projects, partnering with technical teams, clients, and internal stakeholders. This role focuses on Proactive Service, Digital Forensics, and Incident Response engagements to optimize client security posture. You will leverage your project management expertise to ensure mission-critical solutions are delivered efficiently, exceeding customer expectations in a dynamic technical environment.
q: 7+ years of professional experience in Project Management within Cybersecurity, Digital Forensics, or Artificial Intelligence.
Bachelor’s degree in MIS, Cybersecurity, Computer Science, or equivalent work experience.
Proven ability to lead multiple large-scale projects, create plans, and ensure on-time execution.
Demonstrated capacity to work autonomously, prioritize tasks, and solve problems with meticulous attention to detail.
Strong ability to communicate effectively with stakeholders at all levels of client organizations.
Flexibility to work nights, weekends, and holidays as required by incident response engagements.
High level of diplomacy and ability to maintain strict confidentiality.
Previous direct client or customer consulting experience in a technical environment.
PMI Project Management Professional (PMP) certification or equivalent industry credential.
Strong proficiency with project management tools such as Google Suite, Asana, and Clarizen.
